rules.name: Degree Requirements Overview
rules.desc:
Students majoring in International Relations (IR) must complete a minimum of 75 units (30 units of core courses, 40 units of specialization courses, and 5 units of capstone).

• At least one of these courses must be a seminar or colloquium-style class.

• At least one of these courses must be designated as Writing in the Major (WIM) for IR.

rules.name: Required Courses
rules.desc: 5 units in each of the 6 categories below for a total of 30 units.

children.name: American Foreign Policy
children.notes:
INTNLREL 110C or POLISCI 110C can count for the WIM requirement.
INTNLREL 110D, POLISCI 110D, or AMSTUD 110D can count for the WIM requirement.

rules.name: At least one seminar or colloquium-style course
Foreign language through the second year, third quarter, or a proficiency exam

rules.desc:
Students must take a minimum of 40 units of specialization/pathway courses. A minimum of 20 units must be from the student’s primary pathway and a minimum of 15 units from the secondary pathway.
If you complete the minimum 35 primary and secondary pathway units, the remaining five units can be selected from any IR course (pre-approved or petitioned).
Primary and secondary pathways/specializations are not declared on Axess or printed on the diploma or transcript.
Equivalent courses may only be taken for credit once.
rules.notes:
The eleven pathways are:

• Africa

• Comparative International Governance

• East and South Asia

• Economic Development/World Economy

• Environment, Energy, and Natural Resources

• Europe (East and West) & Russia

• International History and Culture

• International Security

• Latin America and Iberian Studies

• Middle East and Central Asia

• Social Development/Human Well-Being

rules.name: WIM Courses

INTNLREL 140C must be taken for 5 units to count for WIM credit.
INTNLREL 200B is open to IR Honors Students only.

children.name: Capstone Paper
children.desc: Students will write an original research paper ideally building on research done in prior coursework. The course (5 units) will provide training on research and writing, interim deadlines for rough drafts, peer review, and opportunities to present the work to other students.

children.name: Capstone Policy Practicum
children.desc: The Practicum offers students hands-on experience in policy-making by having them work in small teams to develop an analysis or recommendation for a client organization. The practicum seminar (5 units) is typically offered in the autumn and winter quarters. Enrollment is limited, and students must submit their applications in advance. Priority will be given to senior students.

children.name: Capstone Project
children.desc: Students will craft their own creative project that could derive from prior coursework, overseas studies, internship, etc. Projects can take a variety of forms such as a collection of op-ed pieces, a podcast, a photo essay, a short documentary film, an educational website, an online exhibit, or a creative writing piece. Students will take a project design course (3 units) that offers skills workshops and peer feedback, followed by an independent course (2 units) to complete their individual projects.

children.name: IR Honors Thesis
children.desc:
The IR Honors program offers qualified students the opportunity to conduct a major independent research project under faculty guidance. Honors application must be made by March of the junior year. All honors students must complete INTNREL 200A/B/C, which starts from the spring of the junior year, as well as INTNREL 198 (Senior Thesis) with their thesis advisors. For details about the program, including examples of past thesis topics, consult the IR Honors Program webpage.
IR Honors students take INTNLREL 198 in the Autumn, Winter, and Spring quarters of their senior year.
IR Honors students may count up to 5 units of IR Honors coursework as capstone units toward their minimum required 75 total major units.

children.name: Interdisciplinary Honors
children.desc: Like departmental honors programs, interdisciplinary honors programs generally require an application, a minimum GPA, and some selected classes, as well as the thesis or capstone project. Most application deadlines are during the winter quarter of junior year, but may range from sophomore spring to senior fall. You may check each program for further details. For IR major capstone credit, prior approval is needed for projects in all interdisciplinary honors programs except the Center for International Security and Cooperation and the Center on Democracy, Development, and the Rule of Law. Students may count up to 5 units of IR capstone pre/approved interdisciplinary honors coursework towards their minimum required 75 total IR major units as long as the interdisciplinary honors program permits double counting their units towards the student's major.

blocks.name: Honors

children.name: INTNLREL 200A, 200B and 200C with a B or better
8 units of INTNLREL 198 over three quarters, B+ or better

blocks.notes:
The International Relations Honors Program offers qualified IR students the opportunity to conduct a significant independent research project under faculty guidance. You may choose a faculty thesis advisor from throughout the university. The program will equip you with the professional “tools” to conduct independent research, analyze the findings, and write a final research thesis. Successfully completing an IR Honors thesis project requires a high degree of initiative, dedication, and a significant investment of time and energy.
The program is interdisciplinary and enables you to undertake various research projects. Previous students have written theses on international political economy, international security, regional integration, human rights, domestic issues in foreign countries, international education, and regional issues. (This list is by no means exhaustive.)
Prerequisites:

• A declared International Relations major with a minimum 3.5 overall grade point average

• Successful experience writing a research paper

• An Honors Thesis proposal

• A thesis advisor

• IR Program approval
Advisor(s):

• Your thesis advisor must be a Stanford Academic Council faculty member. (The IR Office can confirm Academic Council status.)

• Your thesis advisor is responsible for assigning your grade for INTNLREL 198 (see below).
Requirements:

• In spring quarter of your junior year, you will take the INTNLREL 200A: IR Honors Field Research course, which is mandatory for all IR Honors students (3 units).

• In autumn quarter of your senior year, you will enroll in INTNLREL 200B: IR Honors Seminar, which will focus on analyzing research findings and initial steps in writing the thesis (3 units). At the end of the quarter, you should expect to have 1-2 chapters of your thesis submitted in draft form.

• In winter quarter of your senior year, you will take INTNLREL 200C: IR Honors Thesis Writing, in which you will continue to write your honors thesis and present your research (1 unit). You will also receive feedback on your work from Honors cohort members and provide feedback on their work.

• Over the autumn, winter, and spring quarters of your senior year, you will enroll in 8-15 units of INTNLREL 198: Senior Thesis with your Thesis Advisor. Students must enroll in at least one INTNLREL 198 unit each quarter as long as they are enrolled at Stanford University. Unit enrollment will be monitored (Note: INTNLREL 200A/B/C do not count within these 8-15 units).

• Present your thesis findings at the IR Honors Conference in the spring quarter of your senior year (usually in mid-May).

• Complete 15-22 total honors units (200A/B/C and 198). Honors units are taken above and beyond the IR major 70-unit requirement. Note: 200B can satisfy your IR WIM and SEM/COL requirements.
Grading:

• You must receive at least a B+ in INTNLREL 198: Senior Thesis to graduate with honors. If you are making satisfactory progress on your thesis, you will receive an N grade for INTNLREL 198 in the autumn and winter quarters and a final letter grade for spring quarter, which will be retroactively assigned to autumn and winter quarters.

• You must receive at least a B in INTNLREL 200A, INTNLREL 200B, and INTNLREL 200C.
Other Policies:

• You may count up to 5 units of IR Honors coursework as capstone units toward your minimum required 75 total major units.

• If you are not making satisfactory progress with your thesis or otherwise fulfilling the IR Honors thesis program requirements, you may be removed from the program.

• There is no fixed length for your Honors Thesis, but most IR Honors Theses are between 70-100 pages, plus notes and bibliography.

• If you conduct interview or survey research, you must contact the Human Subjects Protocol Panel at http://humansubjects.stanford.edu.

• If you have completed all your IR degree requirements, you may register as Permit for Services Only (PSO) in the spring quarter of your senior year while completing your thesis (international students cannot register for PSO status).

grading:
• All courses that count towards major unit requirements must be taken for a letter grade, and a minimum grade of C is required.

• Foreign language units do not count towards the 75-unit minimum for the major and may be taken for a letter grade or CR/NC.

• Up to two units of IR pre-approved or petitioned courses not offered for a letter grade may be applied toward IR specializations or filler coursework if completed for S grades.
policies:
• A maximum of five units of Directed Reading may be counted toward major units.

• All IR majors must demonstrate proficiency in a foreign language by completing two years of coursework (through the second year, third quarter) or passing a proficiency exam. Students should be aware that they might need at least 15 language units above the university minimum to complete the two-year IR language requirement. Foreign language units do not count towards the 75-unit minimum for the major and may be taken for a letter grade or CR/NC. For more information, please visit the IR website.

• All IR majors must complete one quarter of academic study overseas through Stanford’s Bing Overseas Studies Program (BOSP) or an approved non-Stanford program. Non-Stanford programs must be pre-approved by the IR office before the student enrolls. For more information, please visit the IR website.
transferPolicy: Upon approval by the IR Faculty Director and University Registrar, a maximum of 15 non-Stanford units may be applied to the major for credit. Transfer courses must receive a B- or better to count toward degree requirements.
otherRequirements: 2 yr. foreign lang; Overseas studies 1 qtr.
reviewNotes: The audit checks the 75 units, each letter graded with a C or better (at most 2 S-graded units count): 5 units in each of the six core categories, a primary pathway (20 units) and a secondary pathway (15 units), 5 more units from any pathway list (a petitioned course is moved in by hand), a WIM course and a capstone. For honors it checks INTNLREL 200A-C with a B or better and 8 units of INTNLREL 198 with a B+ or better, and counts at most 5 honors units toward the 75. Foreign language courses never count toward the 75 units, and at most 5 units of directed reading (INTNLREL 197) do. Checked by hand: that the primary and secondary pathways differ, one seminar or colloquium course, foreign language through second year or an exam, one quarter overseas, and up to 15 non-Stanford units with B- or better.
